title: Try Lean's classical tactics on a goal
when: a goal that may be closed by a decision procedure or a normalizer: arithmetic, an identity, an inequality, a finite check
before writing a long proof of a subgoal: see whether omega, linarith, ring, simp, aesop, grind or a hammer closes it
whenNot: the whole problem: the harness already ran this on the target and the subgoals before you started, and says what failed
a goal you cannot state in signature form

statement.description: The goal in signature form: the binders, then : and the proposition, e.g. (n m : ℕ) (h : n < m) : n + 1 ≤ m

header.description: The imports, opens and definitions the statement needs; import Mathlib when not given

cpuBudgetSec.description: Lean time for all tries together, 30 when not given

tactic.description: The tactic that closed the goal

proof.description: The text to put after `by`: Lean's own suggestion when the tactic printed one

domains.description: Where the router put the goal: presburger, linear_real, polynomial_identity, ...

skipped.description: Tactics not tried because the budget ran out or another succeeded

input.statement: (n m : ℕ) (h : n < m) : n + 1 ≤ m

implementations.description: The battery of @seshat/classical over a Lean checker built from the host's Kimina settings: the router names the goal's domain, the tactics the host's Lean has (read by a probe; `packages` names those the profile promises) run in parallel in the order of the router's prior, and the first success stops the rest. Not run against a real Lean.
